arguments.explanation: u_brown, u_orange and line_green were each seated within tolerance at their own place steps and verified conformant at the time. During the final step, place_inverted_u_yellow, the part did not seat (position delta 24.2mm vs 12mm tolerance, orientation delta ~75.6deg vs 10deg tolerance) and the in-hand slip monitor fired, indicating it moved relative to the gripper during the final descent/release. In the same window, the three previously-seated parts and the base1 fixture itself were all disturbed well beyond their tolerances (u_brown 28mm, u_orange 68mm, line_green 86mm, vs 20mm tolerance each), consistent with a collision between the held part/arm and the already-seated assembly during the final seating move. No bystander object (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, base2) was disturbed at any point -- that damage is confined to this assembly's own parts and fixture. Clamp effort never exceeded any part's registry limit and no clamp-effort monitor fired on any part. I did not attempt to reseat the disturbed parts: the scale and simultaneity of the disturbance across the whole board left the root cause (likely an unintended arm path through the seated parts) undiagnosed, and blind reseating of three disturbed parts plus a shifted fixture risked compounding the damage rather than correcting it. base1 and base2 carry no registry tolerance, so their movement is reported qualitatively (base1 observed to shift ~28mm) rather than judged against a verified threshold. The run ends with a standing violation: three previously-conformant parts are now outside tolerance and the fourth was never seated.
